test_cases.title: Program Detail endpoint: bearer-JWT required, RBAC-open, header + 7-card contract, byte-identical across personas
test_cases.given: a program_summary row seeded for program_id=prog-042, and two authenticated sessions differing only by persona (CIO, Engineering Manager)
test_cases.when: GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 is called once per session, plus once with no Authorization header
test_cases.then: the unauthenticated call is rejected, both authenticated calls pass program_visibility and return the seeded header and correctly formatted 7 summary-card values, and the two persona responses are byte-identical
test_cases.objective: Verify the endpoint's full response contract in one pass: bearer-JWT enforcement, the open-aggregate RBAC check with the real program_id, header field sourcing, per-field numeric formatting (6 magnitude fields via format_number, repos ratio unformatted), the FR-PD-17 byte-identical-across-personas invariant, and that no cross-program data leaks into the response.
preconditions: Test database migrated to head; program_summary seeded for program_id='prog-042' with header fields and the 7 raw metric columns
Two valid bearer JWTs available: one resolving to the cio persona, one resolving to engineering-manager with session.programs including 'prog-042'
No test double stubs the handler's persona logic -- this exercises the shipped handler directly

test_data.seeded_description: Core platform migration to the harness pipeline

steps: Seed program_summary for program_id='prog-042' with the header and 7 raw metric values from test_data
Call GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 with no Authorization header
Call GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 with the CIO bearer token
Call GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 with the Engineering Manager bearer token
Diff the CIO and EM response bodies byte-for-byte
Inspect the handler/service source under test for any persona-conditional branch (grep for session.persona/role checks in the code path)
expected_results: The unauthenticated call returns 401 -- bearer-JWT is required, not client-side-only gating
Both authenticated calls return 200, not 403 -- program_visibility passed without checking program_id against session.programs
Both responses' header fields (name, type, description, icon) equal the seeded values
token_consumption == '2.5M', commands_executed == '8.5K', lines_of_code_generated == '125.0K' -- each computed via format_number, not string-built ad hoc
features_delivered == '45', releases_done == '12', user_stories_delivered == '320' -- bare int, no suffix, per format_number's <1000 rule
repos_with_harness_installed renders as '5 / 6', not passed through format_number
The CIO and EM response bodies are byte-identical
No persona-conditional branch exists in the request path
The response JSON contains only header + 7 summary-card fields -- no session.programs or other cross-program data

test_cases.title: Unknown program_id returns the standard 404 JSON error envelope
test_cases.given: no program_summary row exists for program_id=prog-404
test_cases.when: GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-404 is called with a valid bearer token
test_cases.then: the response is 404 with the app's existing single error envelope, matching every other exception handler in the codebase -- no new envelope shape is introduced
test_cases.objective: Verify an unknown program_id fails closed with the existing app-wide error envelope (app/core/errors.py) rather than a bespoke shape or a 200 with empty/null card values.
preconditions: Test database migrated to head; no program_summary row exists for program_id='prog-404'
A valid bearer token for any persona -- RBAC is open-aggregate, so the negative outcome under test is 404-for-unknown-id, not RBAC denial
steps: Call GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-404 with a valid bearer token
Compare the body's top-level shape against another already-shipped 404 response elsewhere in the codebase for structural parity
expected_results: HTTP status is 404
Response body is exactly {"error": {"code": "http_404", "message": <string>, "details": <any>}} -- a single top-level 'error' key, no additional top-level keys
message is a human-readable string containing no internal identifiers or stack-trace content
The shape matches the codebase's existing single error envelope -- no new 404 shape was introduced for this endpoint

test_cases.title: Program Detail page: switcher reloads in place, back-link navigates, error state on unknown program, switcher/back controls are keyboard- and screen-reader-addressable
test_cases.given: the /programs/[program_id] route is rendered for a valid program_id with GET /api/overview/program-detail/{program_id} and GET /api/programs mocked at the fetch boundary
test_cases.when: the user selects a different program in 'Switch program', activates '← Back to program board', and the route is rendered for a program_id whose mock 404s
test_cases.then: selecting a program re-fetches the detail endpoint for the new id and re-renders header/cards in place with the URL updated client-side (no full navigation), the back-link navigates to the Adoption Overview route, the 404 fixture renders an error state instead of a blank shell, and the switcher trigger and back-link expose a correct accessible role/name and respond to keyboard activation
test_cases.objective: Verify the frontend-owned behaviours of the shell in one page-level integration test: switcher reload without full navigation (AC-5/FR-4), back-navigation target (AC-4), error-state rendering for an unknown program instead of a blank shell (AC-7), and baseline keyboard/aria affordances on the switcher and back-link (NFR-008 accessibility, 'where feasible').
preconditions: Fetch mock (e.g. MSW) configured: GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 -> 200 fixture A, GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-099 -> 200 fixture B, GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-404 -> 404 error envelope, GET /api/programs -> a persona-scoped list containing prog-042 and prog-099
next/navigation's router mocked so route changes can be asserted without a real Next.js server
steps: Render the /programs/[program_id] route for program_id='prog-042'; wait for the initial fetch to resolve
Open the 'Switch program' selector and select the option for program_id='prog-099'
Assert a new fetch to /api/overview/program-detail/prog-099 fired and the header/cards re-render with fixture B's values
Activate the '← Back to program board' link
Re-render the route for program_id='prog-404' (the unknown-id fixture) and wait for the fetch to resolve
Query the switcher trigger and back-link for their accessible role and name, and dispatch a keyboard Enter/Space on the switcher trigger
expected_results: After the initial render, the header and 7 cards show fixture A's values

After switching, exactly one new fetch to /api/overview/program-detail/prog-099 occurred, the header/cards now show fixture B's values, and the URL becomes /programs/prog-099 via client-side routing (router.push/replace, not a hard navigation)
Activating the back-link invokes the router toward the Adoption Overview route ('/') rather than a hard browser navigation
The prog-404 render shows a distinct error state, not the empty/blank card shell
The switcher trigger exposes an accessible name and a role/attribute pair consistent with its expanded/collapsed state (e.g. aria-haspopup/aria-expanded), and Enter/Space opens the option list
The back-link renders as a real anchor/button with an accessible name containing 'Back to program board', not a bare clickable div

test_cases.title: Program Detail request stays within its single-query performance budget and emits the program_drilldown observability event
test_cases.given: a seeded program_summary row for program_id=prog-042 and a query counter/spy attached to the test database session
test_cases.then: exactly one bounded select() runs against program_summary with no N+1 fan-out, the handler completes well inside its latency budget, and a structured JSON program_drilldown log event fires once with {program_id: 'prog-042'} and no PII
test_cases.objective: Verify the endpoint's performance contract as scoped by NFR-performance (one bounded select, no unbounded fan-out -- the concrete, testable form of the story's 3s page-render budget for the backend leg) and the program_drilldown half of FR-5/NFR-observability, in one request/response cycle. Full end-to-end page-render timing is not exercised here -- no e2e framework is configured (test_e2e is empty) -- this measures the endpoint's own bounded latency and query count as the backend's share of that budget. The program_switch half of FR-5 ({from_program_id, to_program_id} on switcher selection) is not independently exercised: the PRD does not specify how the backend distinguishes a switcher-triggered fetch from an initial page load, and no mechanism is fabricated here to test it.
preconditions: Test database migrated to head; program_summary seeded for program_id='prog-042'
A query counter or session-level spy attached for the duration of the call
Log capture attached over the endpoint's logger, filtering for the program_drilldown event
A valid bearer token for any persona
steps: Attach the query counter and log capture
Call GET /api/overview/program-detail/prog-042 with a valid bearer token, timing the call
Inspect the query counter and the captured log records
expected_results: Exactly one SELECT ran against program_summary for the call -- no N+1 fan-out
The handler's own duration is under the budget recorded in test_data (proxy for the page's 3s render budget; frontend/network legs are out of this backend test's reach)
Exactly one program_drilldown log record was emitted, structured JSON, with program_id == 'prog-042' and no other request/user content
The log record carries no PII (no email, name, or raw request content)

budget.target: exactly 1 SELECT against program_summary AND handler duration < 500ms (test_data query_count_budget/handler_duration_budget_ms; backend proxy for story NFR-001's 3s page-render budget)

audit_notes: FR-1 splits across two TCs: TC-01 exercises the RBAC-call-with-real-id half, TC-04 exercises the single-bounded-select/no-N+1 half -- together they cover FR-1's full definition.

NFR-security has no dedicated type:security TC under the 4-case cap; its bearer-JWT-required and program_visibility-gate clauses (including a no-token-401 sub-case) are genuinely exercised inside TC-01 (type: contract) instead.

FR-5 / NFR-observability are only partially exercised: TC-04 asserts the program_drilldown event shape, which is fully specified in the PRD. The program_switch event's trigger mechanism (how the backend distinguishes a switcher-triggered fetch from an initial page load) is not specified anywhere in the PRD or story, so no test asserts it -- fabricating a mechanism to close this gap was judged worse than disclosing it. This is a specification gap, not a test-authoring omission.

AC-2 and AC-3 are primarily covered by TC-01 (real backend data, real formatting); TC-03's coverage of them is incidental (a mocked-fixture render used to set up the switcher scenario), listed as a secondary coverer for transparency, not as independent proof of the real backend contract.

No unit-shaped cases appear here by design (test-case-generation skill, Scope section): ProgramDetailHeader.tsx, ProgramSummaryCards.tsx, ProgramSwitcher.tsx, BackToProgramBoard.tsx component tests belong in docs/features/PGD-01/tasks.json, per the story's own Test mapping section.
